fullPassage:
Pictures Worth a Thousand Words

As quickly as a camera captures a scene, an image can grab hold of our emotions. Through speech or written text, it can be difficult to convey a complex message quickly. Yet photographs can change people's hearts and minds in an instant. And when the magic of photography sparks an emotional reaction in a great number of people, it can change history.

The Burning River That Started a Movement

In the 1880s, industry began to grow rapidly along the Cuyahoga River in the city of Cleveland. This industrial growth provided steady jobs to people in the area. Meanwhile, steel mills and factories started dumping large amounts of waste into the river. Although the river became polluted, most people simply regarded this as a sign of the area's economic success.

In June 1969, the polluted river caught fire. The likely cause was a burning flare falling from a train, which set fire to oil-soaked waste beneath a bridge. At that time, few people in Cleveland cared. This was because fires had been recorded on the Cuyahoga more than ten times before, and some of them had been much worse.

However, it wasn't long before the 1969 fire became famous. This was thanks to an article published in Time magazine that year. The article featured a shocking photograph of flames and smoke rising from the river. But this was not a photograph of the 1969 fire, which was put out so quickly that nobody took a picture of it. In fact, it was a picture of a much worse fire that had occurred on the river several years earlier. Still, the image had a great impact on people.

Around that time, the attitudes of Americans toward environmental problems were starting to change. More and more people were becoming aware of the need to protect the environment, and the shocking image of the burning river sparked public anger about water pollution. As a result, the Cuyahoga River fire of 1969 became a symbol of pollution. A national environmental awareness event was held on April 22, 1970, which later became known as the first Earth Day. And in 1972, national water quality standards were established with the passage of the Clean Water Act.

Exposing the Harsh Reality of Child Labor

In the 19th century, the Industrial Revolution led to a dramatic increase in factory production in the United States. The demand for workers increased, and many new positions were filled by children. By 1900, about twenty percent of all children in the United States were employed, and some of those working in factories were only four years old. The work was difficult and dangerous, leaving many child laborers with health problems.

Factory owners turned to child labor for several reasons. For example, children could be paid less than adult workers. They were also less likely to go on strike.

Lewis Hine, a teacher and photographer, wanted to reveal how cruel this system was. So he quit his teaching job and started to work for the National Child Labor Committee as an investigative photographer. He gained access to factories by pretending to have different jobs like insurance agent or fire inspector.

Once inside, he would photograph the children working there. He would also ask their names and ages and record information about their living and working conditions. From 1908 to 1912, he secretly gathered information and took photographs to expose factory owners who were taking advantage of helpless children.

Hine's photographs captured young children doing all sorts of jobs. These included picking vegetables, weaving baskets, and even handling dangerous equipment. What is more, the children's faces showed the tragic impact of hard labor. When people saw the children's joyless expressions, they could not help but feel heartbroken.

The pictures were later shown in exhibitions, lectures, magazine articles, and so on. As a result, the public realized just how serious the situation was. Soon, many states passed stronger laws to ban the employment of children. In 1938, the United States Congress passed an act that made it illegal for children under sixteen to work in factories during school hours.

These examples show that photographs can bring meaningful change to society. They prove that, sometimes, a picture truly is worth a thousand words.

questions.passage: As quickly as a camera captures a scene, an image can grab hold of our emotions. Through speech or written text, it can be difficult to (A)[convey / convert] a complex message quickly. Yet photographs can change people's hearts and minds in an (B)[instant / instance]. And when the magic of photography (C)[sparks / speaks] an emotional reaction in a great number of people, it can change history. The Burning River That Started a Movement In the 1880s, industry began to grow rapidly along the Cuyahoga River in the city of Cleveland. This industrial growth provided steady jobs to people in the area.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 연설이나 글로 쓰인 텍스트를 통해 복잡한 메시지를 빠르게 전달하는 것은 어려울 수 있다. 사진은 순식간에 사람들의 마음을 바꿀 수 있다. 사진 촬영의 마법이 감정적 반응을 촉발할 때 역사를 바꿀 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① convey — instant — sparks
❌ ② convert — instance — speaks
❌ ③ convey — instance — speaks
❌ ④ convert — instant — sparks
✅ (A) convey: '전달하다'로 메시지를 전하는 문맥에 적합. convert(변환하다)는 메시지와 어울리지 않음. ✅ (B) instant: 'in an instant(순식간에)'는 관용 표현. instance(사례)는 문맥 불일치. ✅ (C) sparks: '촉발하다'로 감정적 반응을 일으키는 문맥에 적합. speaks(말하다)는 목적어로 reaction을 취하지 않음.
det.tip: convey a message: 메시지를 전달하다. in an instant: 순식간에. spark a reaction: 반응을 촉발하다.

questions.passage: Yet photographs can change people's hearts and minds in an instant. And when the magic of photography sparks an emotional reaction in a great number of people, it can change history. In the 1880s, industry began to grow (A)[rapidly / rarely] along the Cuyahoga River in the city of Cleveland. This industrial growth provided (B)[steady / steep] jobs to people in the area. Meanwhile, steel mills and factories started (C)[dumping / jumping] large amounts of waste into the river. Although the river became polluted, most people simply regarded this as a sign of the area's economic success.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 1880년대에 산업이 쿠야호가 강을 따라 빠르게 성장하기 시작했다. 이러한 산업 성장은 사람들에게 안정적인 일자리를 제공했다. 한편, 제철소와 공장은 대량의 폐기물을 강에 버리기 시작했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① rarely — steep — dumping
✅ ② rapidly — steady — dumping
❌ ③ rapidly — steep — jumping
❌ ④ rarely — steady — jumping
✅ (A) rapidly: '빠르게' 성장. rarely(거의 ~않는)는 성장 문맥과 반대. ✅ (B) steady: '안정적인' 일자리. steep(가파른)은 jobs와 어울리지 않음. ✅ (C) dumping: 폐기물을 '버리다'. jumping(뛰다)은 waste와 어울리지 않음.
det.tip: rapidly: 빠르게 (= quickly). steady jobs: 안정적인 일자리. dump waste: 폐기물을 투기하다.

questions.passage: For example, children could be paid less than adult workers. They were also less likely to go on strike. Lewis Hine, a teacher and photographer, wanted to (A)[reveal / relieve] how cruel this system was. So he quit his teaching job and started to work for the National Child Labor Committee as an (B)[investigative / innovative] photographer. He gained access to factories by (C)[pretending / intending] to have different jobs like insurance agent or fire inspector. Once inside, he would photograph the children working there.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 교사이자 사진작가인 루이스 하인은 이 제도가 얼마나 잔인한지 밝히고 싶었다. 전국아동노동위원회에서 탐사 사진작가로 일하기 시작했다. 보험 설계사나 화재 조사관 같은 다른 직업을 가진 것처럼 가장함으로써 공장에 접근했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① relieve — investigative — intending
❌ ② reveal — innovative — intending
✅ ③ reveal — investigative — pretending
❌ ④ relieve — innovative — pretending
✅ (A) reveal: 잔인한 제도를 '폭로하다'. relieve(안심시키다)는 문맥과 반대. ✅ (B) investigative: '탐사' 사진작가. innovative(혁신적인)는 잠입 조사 문맥과 맞지 않음. ✅ (C) pretending: 다른 직업인 '척하며'. intending(의도하다)은 'to have different jobs'와 의미 불일치.
det.tip: reveal vs relieve: 철자 유사하지만 reveal(드러내다) ≠ relieve(완화하다). investigative photographer: 탐사 보도 사진기자.

questions.passage: In ①<u>June</u> 1969, the polluted river caught fire. The ②<u>likely</u> cause was a burning flare falling from a train, which set fire to oil-soaked waste beneath a bridge. At ③<u>that</u> time, few people in Cleveland <u>cared</u>. ④<u>This</u> was because fires had been <u>recorded</u> on the Cuyahoga more than ten times before, and some of them had been much <u>worse</u>. However, it wasn't long before the 1969 fire became <u>forgotten</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 뜻이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 1969년 6월 오염된 강에 불이 붙었다. 클리블랜드에서는 관심을 가진 사람이 거의 없었다. 이전에 열 번 넘게 화재가 기록되었고 일부는 훨씬 더 심했기 때문이다. 하지만 머지않아 1969년 화재가 유명해졌다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ①
❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
✅ ④ ④
④ forgotten(잊혀진) → famous(유명해진): 원문에서 1969년 화재는 타임지 기사 덕분에 '유명해졌다'고 했으므로 forgotten은 문맥과 반대. ① cared: 관심을 가진 사람이 적었다(적절). ② recorded: 화재가 기록되었다(적절). ③ worse: 일부 화재가 더 심했다(적절).
det.tip: 문맥상 부적절한 어휘 문제: 전체 흐름에서 역접 관계(However)를 파악하면 정답을 찾기 쉽다.

questions.passage: ①<u>Around</u> that time, the attitudes of Americans toward environmental problems were starting to change. ②<u>More</u> and more people were becoming <u>aware</u> of the need to protect the environment, and the shocking image of the burning river sparked public <u>anger</u> about water pollution. As a ③<u>result</u>, the Cuyahoga River fire of 1969 became a <u>symbol</u> of pollution. A ④<u>national</u> environmental awareness event was held on April 22, 1970, which later became known as the first Earth Day. And in 1972, national water quality standards were <u>abandoned</u> with the passage of the Clean Water Act.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 뜻이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 환경 문제에 대한 미국인들의 태도가 바뀌기 시작했다. 환경을 보호할 필요성을 인지하게 되었고, 불타는 강의 이미지는 대중의 분노를 촉발시켰다. 쿠야호가 강 화재는 오염의 상징이 되었다. 1972년 청정수법의 통과와 함께 국가 수질 기준이 수립되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ ④
❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
❌ ① ①
④ abandoned(폐기된) → established(수립된): 원문에서 수질 기준이 '수립되었다'고 했으므로, abandoned(폐기된)는 정반대 의미. ① aware: 필요성을 인지하게 되었다(적절). ② anger: 대중의 분노를 촉발했다(적절). ③ symbol: 오염의 상징이 되었다(적절).
det.tip: established vs abandoned: 법률/기준 문맥에서 establish(수립)와 abandon(폐기)은 정반대.

questions.passage: ①<u>Once</u> inside, he ②<u>would</u> photograph the children working there. He would also ask their names and ages and record information about their living and working conditions. ③<u>From</u> 1908 to 1912, he secretly gathered information and took photographs to <u>expose</u> factory owners who were taking <u>advantage</u> of helpless children. ④<u>Hine</u>'s photographs captured young children doing all sorts of jobs. These included picking vegetables, weaving baskets, and even <u>handling</u> dangerous equipment. What is more, the children's faces showed the <u>cheerful</u> impact of hard labor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 뜻이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 그는 무력한 아이들을 이용하던 공장주들을 폭로하기 위해 몰래 정보를 수집하고 사진을 찍었다. 하인의 사진은 채소 따기, 바구니 짜기, 심지어 위험한 장비를 다루는 일까지 포함했다. 아이들의 얼굴은 고된 노동의 비극적인 영향을 보여주었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ①
❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
✅ ④ ④
④ cheerful(즐거운) → tragic(비극적인): 원문에서 아이들의 얼굴이 고된 노동의 '비극적인' 영향을 보여줬다고 했으므로 cheerful은 정반대. ① expose: 폭로하다(적절). ② advantage: 이용하다(take advantage of)(적절). ③ handling: 위험한 장비를 다루다(적절).
det.tip: tragic vs cheerful: 아동 노동의 가혹한 현실을 묘사하는 맥락에서 cheerful(밝은)은 어울리지 않음.

questions.passage: As quickly as a camera captures a scene, an image can grab hold of our emotions. Through speech or written text, it can be difficult to convey a complex message quickly. Yet photographs can change people's hearts and minds in an instant. And when the magic of photography sparks an emotional reaction in a great number of people, it can change __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 카메라가 장면을 포착하는 것만큼 빠르게 이미지는 감정을 사로잡을 수 있다. 사진이 많은 사람들에게 감정적 반응을 일으킬 때, 그것은 __________를 바꿀 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① fashion
✅ ② history
❌ ③ weather
❌ ④ language
✅ history(역사): 본문 전체가 사진이 사회 변화(역사)를 이끈 사례를 다루고 있으므로, '역사를 바꿀 수 있다'가 글의 핵심 주제와 일치. fashion(유행), weather(날씨), language(언어)는 본문 내용과 무관.
det.tip: change history: 역사를 바꾸다. 글 전체의 주제를 파악하면 빈칸을 쉽게 채울 수 있다.

questions.passage: However, it wasn't long before the 1969 fire became famous. This was thanks to an article published in Time magazine that year. The article featured a shocking photograph of flames and smoke rising from the river. But this was not a photograph of the 1969 fire, which was put out so quickly that nobody took a picture of it. In fact, it was a picture of a much worse fire that had occurred on the river several years earlier. Still, the image had a great __________ on people.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 머지않아 1969년 화재가 유명해졌다. 타임지에 실린 충격적인 사진 덕분이었다. 그 사진은 사실 몇 년 전 더 심한 화재의 것이었다. 그럼에도 그 이미지는 사람들에게 큰 __________을/를 주었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① impact
❌ ② discount
❌ ③ silence
❌ ④ distance
✅ impact(영향): 'have a great impact on(~에 큰 영향을 미치다)'은 원문의 표현 그대로. discount(할인), silence(침묵), distance(거리)는 문맥과 전혀 맞지 않음.
det.tip: have an impact on: ~에 영향을 미치다. great/huge/significant impact처럼 형용사와 함께 자주 쓰인다.

questions.passage: Factory owners turned to child labor for several reasons. For example, children could be paid less than adult workers. They were also less likely to go on strike. Lewis Hine, a teacher and photographer, wanted to reveal how cruel this system was. So he quit his teaching job and started to work for the National Child Labor Committee as an investigative photographer. He gained __________ to factories by pretending to have different jobs like insurance agent or fire inspector.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 공장주들은 여러 이유로 아동 노동에 의존했다. 루이스 하인은 이 잔인한 제도를 폭로하고 싶어 탐사 사진작가로 일했다. 그는 보험 설계사나 화재 조사관인 척하며 공장에 __________을/를 얻었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① permission
❌ ② opposition
✅ ③ access
❌ ④ resistance
✅ access(접근): 'gain access to(~에 대한 접근을 얻다)'는 원문 표현. permission(허가)은 '가장'해서 얻은 것이므로 부적합. opposition(반대), resistance(저항)는 문맥과 무관.
det.tip: gain access to: ~에 접근하다/~에 대한 접근권을 얻다. access는 명사로 '접근, 이용권'의 의미.

questions.passage: Meanwhile, steel mills and factories started dumping large amounts of waste into the river. Although the river became polluted, most people simply <u>regarded</u> this as a sign of the area's economic success. In June 1969, the polluted river caught fire. The likely cause was a burning flare falling from a train, which set fire to oil-soaked waste beneath a bridge.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 regarded와 의미가 가장 유사한 것은?

det.korean: 비록 강이 오염되긴 했지만, 대부분의 사람들은 이를 단순히 그 지역의 경제적 성공의 신호로 여겼다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ignored
❌ ② rejected
❌ ③ analyzed
✅ ④ considered
✅ considered(여기다, 간주하다): regarded는 '~으로 여기다/간주하다'의 뜻으로 considered와 동의어. ignored(무시하다), rejected(거부하다), analyzed(분석하다)는 의미가 다름.
det.tip: regard A as B = consider A (as) B: A를 B로 여기다/간주하다.

questions.passage:
And in 1972, national water quality standards were established with the passage of the Clean Water Act. Exposing the Harsh Reality of Child Labor

In the 19th century, the Industrial Revolution led to a <u>dramatic</u> increase in factory production in the United States. The demand for workers increased, and many new positions were filled by children. By 1900, about twenty percent of all children in the United States were employed, and some of those working in factories were only four years old.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 dramatic과 의미가 가장 유사한 것은?

det.korean: 19세기에 산업혁명은 미국의 공장 생산량의 극적인 증가로 이어졌다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① minor
✅ ② striking
❌ ③ gradual
❌ ④ fictional
✅ striking(눈에 띄는, 극적인): dramatic은 '극적인, 인상적인' 뜻으로 striking과 유사. minor(사소한)은 반의어. gradual(점진적인)은 반대 뉘앙스. fictional(허구의)은 무관.
det.tip: dramatic increase: 급격한 증가. dramatic은 '연극의'뿐 아니라 '극적인, 눈에 띄는'이라는 뜻도 있다.

questions.passage: The pictures were later shown in exhibitions, lectures, magazine articles, and so on. As a result, the public realized just how serious the situation was. Soon, many states passed stronger laws to <u>ban</u> the employment of children.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ban과 의미가 가장 유사한 것은?

det.korean: 그 사진들은 전시회, 강연, 잡지 기사 등에 공개되었다. 그 결과 대중은 상황의 심각성을 깨달았고, 많은 주가 아동 고용을 금지하기 위해 더 강력한 법안을 통과시켰다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① prohibit
❌ ② promote
❌ ③ maintain
❌ ④ encourage
✅ prohibit(금지하다): ban은 '금지하다'로 prohibit과 동의어. promote(촉진하다), maintain(유지하다), encourage(장려하다)는 모두 반대 의미.
det.tip: ban = prohibit = forbid: 모두 '금지하다'라는 의미. ban은 법적 금지에 자주 사용.

questions.passage: He gained access to factories by pretending to have different jobs like insurance agent or fire inspector. Once inside, he would photograph the children working there. He would also ask their names and ages and record information about their living and working conditions. From 1908 to 1912, he <u>secretly</u> gathered information and took photographs to expose factory owners who were taking advantage of helpless children.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 secretly와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

questions.passage:
Pictures Worth a Thousand Words

As quickly as a camera captures a scene, an image can grab hold of our emotions. Through speech or written text, it can be difficult to convey a complex message quickly. Yet photographs can change people's hearts and minds in an instant. And when the magic of photography sparks an emotional reaction in a great number of people, it can change history.

The Burning River That Started a Movement

In the 1880s, industry began to grow rapidly along the Cuyahoga River in the city of Cleveland. This industrial growth provided steady jobs to people in the area. Meanwhile, steel mills and factories started dumping large amounts of waste into the river. Although the river became polluted, most people simply regarded this as a sign of the area's economic success.

In June 1969, the polluted river caught fire. The likely cause was a burning flare falling from a train, which set fire to oil-soaked waste beneath a bridge. At that time, few people in Cleveland cared. This was because fires had been recorded on the Cuyahoga more than ten times before, and some of them had been much worse.

However, it wasn't long before the 1969 fire became famous. This was thanks to an article published in Time magazine that year. The article featured a shocking photograph of flames and smoke rising from the river. But this was not a photograph of the 1969 fire, which was put out so quickly that nobody took a picture of it. In fact, it was a picture of a much worse fire that had occurred on the river several years earlier. Still, the image had a great impact on people.

Around that time, the attitudes of Americans toward environmental problems were starting to change. More and more people were becoming aware of the need to protect the environment, and the shocking image of the burning river sparked public anger about water pollution. As a result, the Cuyahoga River fire of 1969 became a symbol of pollution. A national environmental awareness event was held on April 22, 1970, which later became known as the first Earth Day. And in 1972, national water quality standards were established with the passage of the Clean Water Act.

Exposing the Harsh Reality of Child Labor

In the 19th century, the Industrial Revolution led to a dramatic increase in factory production in the United States. The demand for workers increased, and many new positions were filled by children. By 1900, about twenty percent of all children in the United States were employed, and some of those working in factories were only four years old. The work was difficult and dangerous, leaving many child laborers with health problems.

Factory owners turned to child labor for several reasons. For example, children could be paid less than adult workers. They were also less likely to go on strike.

Lewis Hine, a teacher and photographer, wanted to reveal how cruel this system was. So he quit his teaching job and started to work for the National Child Labor Committee as an investigative photographer. He gained access to factories by pretending to have different jobs like insurance agent or fire inspector.

Once inside, he would photograph the children working there. He would also ask their names and ages and record information about their living and working conditions. From 1908 to 1912, he secretly gathered information and took photographs to expose factory owners who were taking advantage of helpless children.

Hine's photographs captured young children doing all sorts of jobs. These included picking vegetables, weaving baskets, and even handling dangerous equipment. What is more, the children's faces showed the tragic impact of hard labor. When people saw the children's joyless expressions, they could not help but feel heartbroken.

The pictures were later shown in exhibitions, lectures, magazine articles, and so on. As a result, the public realized just how serious the situation was. Soon, many states passed stronger laws to ban the employment of children. In 1938, the United States Congress passed an act that made it illegal for children under sixteen to work in factories during school hours.

These examples show that photographs can bring meaningful change to society. They prove that, sometimes, a picture truly is worth a thousand words.
